detail.title: Synthesis of Consensus Reliability and Architectural Accountability
detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes foundational principles of independent judgment in autonomous systems and commits further research to refine assumption testing and consensus weighting.

children.title: formal criteria for independent agent evidence reliability versus expert consensus

detail.reason: Establishing a decision-theoretic framework requires analyzing conditions under which internal model output reliably corrects external expert error.

children.title: distinction between foundational system assumptions and operational heuristics in self-modifying models

detail.reason: Clarifying the boundary between modifiable heuristics and rigid foundational assumptions is required to advance the assumption testing project.

detail.title: Independent Judgment versus Consensus Reliability
detail.summary: Consensus reliability depends not merely on majority weight but on the formal independence of evidence sources. Intelligent systems should prioritize independent verification over consensus when the latter exhibits correlated error structures.
detail.reason: Establishing an epistemic framework for disagreement with consensus is essential for autonomous integrity.
